title: Within Tolerance
passage:
Every dimple pattern on the market is advertised as a design. At the Kilnbeck test tunnel, where balls are fired past a laser gate at ninety metres a second, the patterns matter less than the catalogues suggest. Depth is what the tunnel notices: a dimple shallower by twelve microns behaves almost like no dimple at all, and twelve microns is inside the drift of a mould across a single production run. Jorunn Steinvik, who runs the tunnel, will not go so far as to call the arrangements decorative — hexagonal packing does buy a little, she thinks, at the margins. What she will say is that two balls lifted from the same box can differ more, in the tunnel, than two rival designs differ on paper. The number printed on the sleeve, 332 or 392, is the one figure she has never seen matter.
— Halvard Ekstrand, science pages

questions.prompt: What is implied about the dimple patterns that ball makers advertise?

options.text: That deeper dimples tend to give a longer flight than shallow ones at the same speed.
That makers pick their patterns to survive the wear of the moulds they are pressed in.
That the gap between rival patterns can be smaller than the variation inside one box.
That the arrangement of the dimples has no bearing on the way a ball flies.

questions.rationale: TYPE-002 inference, one logical inch beyond the tunnel's two findings. The passage never ranks the advertised patterns against each other directly; it reports that depth is what the tunnel notices, that twelve microns of depth is inside the drift of a mould across one production run, and that 'two balls lifted from the same box can differ more, in the tunnel, than two rival designs differ on paper'. Putting those together gives C: the advertised difference between patterns is smaller than the unadvertised difference within a single box. A = too_far; the passage says a dimple shallower by twelve microns behaves almost like no dimple, which establishes that depth matters near a threshold, not that flight lengthens steadily with depth — the text offers no comparison of deeper against shallower balls in flight. B = reversed relationship; mould wear appears in the passage as the source of the variation that swamps the design, never as a criterion the makers design around, and nothing is said about how patterns are chosen. D = quantifier upgrade of Steinvik's hedge; she explicitly declines to call the arrangements decorative and grants that 'hexagonal packing does buy a little ... at the margins', so 'no bearing' overshoots the one stance the text is careful to qualify. Hedge balance: A hedges with 'tend to' and C with 'can be', so the measured option is not uniquely the key; the key is 15 words against 16/16/15, so it is not the longest.
